content:
The test image shows a soybean leaf with numerous small, scattered yellow-green spots distributed across the entire upper leaf surface. Spots are tiny, round, and appear as pale/yellowish dots on dark green tissue. No large necrotic lesions, no brown margins visible.

Top candidates: Bacterial_Pustule (small pustules with yellow halos), Downy_mildew (yellow spots on upper surface), Soybean_rust (small spots/pustules).

The Bacterial_Pustule reference shows brown/orange pustules with vein-bordered necrosis — doesn't match the test image's small scattered yellow-green dots on a green leaf.

Reassessing: The test image shows tiny, uniformly scattered yellow-green spots on the upper leaf surface of an otherwise green, healthy-looking leaf. This pattern is most consistent with **Downy_mildew**, which causes pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface (with corresponding grayish sporulation underneath). Soybean rust typically shows tan/brown uredinia on the underside.
